rendered:
The sodiation of the carbon layer provides 0.05 mAh/cm^2[1] of areal capacity, 120 mAh/g[2] on a mass basis. The paper calls this negligible[3] compared with the plating capacities, which reach up to 12 mAh/cm^2[4] in this work. The labels in the sodiation-and-plating figure show the same contrast: 0.05[5] for sodiation and 12[6] for plating. So the meaningful capacity comes from the in situ plating of sodium metal, not from the carbon sodiation.

For reference, the plating loadings in the plating-and-stripping tests run from 0.5 mAh/cm^2[7] (the shorter plating time) up to 8 mAh/cm^2[8] (the longest plating time), and the cycling tests used 12 mAh/cm^2[9], all far above the sodiation capacity.
